name: CV / Resume Analysis - API Designer
description: Signals extracted from the user's CV/resume to evidence API Designer skills. CV data provides self-reported information that must be cross-validated with GitHub and assessment sources. Focus on organizational API governance, platform architecture, and strategic design leadership — not individual service implementation.

extraction_rules.description: How to extract and weight information from CV content for API Design roles.

sections.description: Explicit list of API design tools, specifications, and governance frameworks mentioned in skills section.
sections.notes: Low strength because listing 'OpenAPI' or 'GraphQL' alone doesn't prove governance expertise. Look for governance-specific tools like Spectral, Backstage, or Apigee.

sections.description: Job descriptions mentioning API architecture, governance, and platform-level design activities.
sections.notes: Higher strength when specific governance outcomes, API portfolio scale, and architectural decisions are described.
quality_indicators: Organizational scope indicators (e.g., 'established API standards across 15 engineering teams', 'governed 200+ APIs')
Governance tooling and process establishment (e.g., 'implemented Spectral linting in CI/CD', 'launched API design review board')
API strategy and business alignment language (e.g., 'drove API-first strategy', 'reduced time-to-integration by 60%')
Multi-protocol design experience (REST, GraphQL, gRPC, AsyncAPI mentioned in architectural context)

sections.description: API platform projects, developer portal implementations, or API governance tool contributions.
sections.notes: Higher strength if linked to open-source API governance tools, published API style guides, or developer portal implementations.
quality_indicators: Technical depth of API governance project (e.g., 'built Spectral custom ruleset with 50+ organization-specific rules')
Developer portal or documentation platform architecture
API gateway or service mesh architecture contributions
Published API style guides or governance frameworks

sections.description: Relevant degrees in software engineering, computer science, or distributed systems.
sections.notes: Provides theoretical foundation but API design governance expertise is primarily learned through practice.

sections.description: Professional certifications relevant to API design and management.
sections.notes: Certifications indicate theoretical domain knowledge; cross-validate with governance artifacts and assessment.

signal_mapping.description: How CV mentions map to skill evidence using COMPOSITE KEYS ({skill_id}.{subskill_id}). AI should use these patterns.

patterns.pattern: Established organization-wide API style guides and HTTP method/status code standards
Designed REST API resource modeling standards and pagination conventions
Authored API style guides and governed schema evolution compatibility
Evaluated and selected API protocols (REST, GraphQL, gRPC) based on use case analysis
Governed GraphQL federation or managed schema registries for event-driven APIs
Designed OAuth2/OIDC authentication architecture and scope hierarchies for API platforms
Conducted API threat modeling and designed zero-trust API architecture
Designed API rate limiting quota policies and SLA/SLO latency budgets
Architected CDN edge distribution and capacity planning for global API platforms
Established contract testing governance with Pact and consumer-driven contracts
Architected API gateway strategies and service mesh routing for multi-cloud deployments
Managed API versioning policies, deprecation lifecycles, and developer portal experiences
Led API program management and governance councils aligned with business objectives
Has Apigee or MuleSoft certification without governance project evidence

important_notes: CV data is self-reported and inherently unreliable as standalone evidence
Always cross-validate CV claims with GitHub governance artifacts and adaptive assessment results
Distinguish governance scope — 'designed APIs' (individual contributor) differs from 'established API standards across teams' (governance leader)
Look for organizational impact indicators — number of APIs governed, teams standardized, time-to-integration improvements
Recency and scale matter — governing 200+ APIs at a large platform company differs from writing OpenAPI specs for a startup's 3 endpoints
API certifications (Apigee, MuleSoft) indicate tool knowledge but not governance leadership
